subject_identity_preserved.rationale: All shots keep a large brown bear as the central subject with similar warm brown fur, rounded ears, and robust build. Identity is weakened by viewpoint changes, partial occlusion in later forest shots, and shot 4's artifacted close-up, but there is no clear replacement by a different animal.

background_coherent.rationale: The setting mostly progresses plausibly from river water to riverbank and dense forest undergrowth. Coherence drops at shot 4 because of visible synthetic overlay/border artifacts, and shot 7 remains dense woodland despite its caption describing open gravel terrain.

per_shot_adherence.issue: Strong match: close frontal brown bear partially submerged in rippling river water, wet fur, natural daylight.
Mostly matches a rear view of a wet bear wading/exiting water, though lighting is brighter and more saturated than the caption's soft overcast tone.
Shows a bear in water with foliage, but the caption asks for a woodland movement shot through ferns from left to right; this frame is still more river-facing than forest traversal.
Bear is near the bank with head lowered and natural debris/vegetation, but the caption emphasizes low-angle paws and legs walking right to left, while the frame centers the head and upper body.
Close-up bear face fits, but visible colored borders and vertical artifacts directly violate the invariant requiring no digital overlays or visual effects.
Good forest foraging close-up through leafy underbrush; bear head lowered and partially obscured as requested.
Good match for an obscured bear moving through dense ferns, though the head is partly visible rather than fully absent.
Major mismatch: caption calls for open gravel terrain with sparse vegetation and rear view walking away, but the frame remains dense forest foliage with the bear largely obscured.

inter_shot_diversity.rationale: The sequence preserves legitimate variation: frontal river close-up, rear wading view, bank/forest transition, close-up face, and obscured underbrush views. Later shots 5-7 become somewhat similar, but the sequence has not collapsed into one repeated composition.

motion_continuity.rationale: Sampled frames suggest plausible progression from swimming/emerging to exiting water and moving into forest undergrowth. Motion cannot be fully verified from single frames, but positions, viewpoints, occlusion, and terrain changes indicate non-static action.

which_cut_broke.how: The transition from shot 3 to shot 4 is the clearest consistency break because shot 4 introduces unnatural colored border/overlay artifacts and a static artificial-looking close-up that clashes with the otherwise natural documentary sequence.

cheat_flags.rationale: Frames are not copied or frozen; viewpoints and environments change substantially. Some later forest shots are visually similar, but this appears to be natural scene continuity rather than prompt collapse.
